entries.name: irq0_vector
entries.comment: ADSP-2100 interrupt vectors: IRQn jumps to PM n (adsp2100.cpp:880). All four are RTI: the program runs without interrupts. IRQ0

entries.name: irq1_vector
entries.comment: IRQ1: RTI

entries.name: irq2_vector
entries.comment: IRQ2: RTI

entries.name: irq3_vector
entries.comment: IRQ3: RTI

entries.name: reset
entries.comment: Reset entry: the ADSP-2100 starts at PM 4 (adsp2100.cpp:636; MAME shows PC 4 while the 68k holds the ADSP in reset). CALL 0780 and CALL 0834 initialise, then L0-L7 = 0, M1 = M7 = 1.

entries.name: frame_loop
entries.comment: Top of the frame loop: 00C2 jumps back here after each frame.

entries.name: wait_frame_trigger
entries.comment: Spins while DM 1FFF reads FFFF (0013-0015): the 68k starts a frame by writing DM 1FFF through 80BFFE, which MAME also turns into a CPU sync (hd68k_adsp_data_w, harddriv_m.cpp:591). docs/01 section 5. [idle read of DM 1FFF, the 68k's frame trigger word (MAME's speedup hooks this read: init_stunrun, hdadsp_speedup_r)]
DM 1FFF = FFFF: re-arms the frame trigger

entries.name: copy_frame_parameters
entries.comment: Copies DM 1FEF-1FF4 to PM 1019-101E, DM 1FF5-1FFD to PM 1000-1008 and DM 1FE9-1FEE to PM 1009-100E: the 68k's per-frame parameters into the PM workspace at 1000-1028 (HYP: view matrix and position; M3).

entries.name: select_object_page
entries.comment: /MP = DM 1FFE: the object ROM page the 68k chose for this frame.
/MP: object ROM page, base = 0x10000 * value (case 7, harddriv_m.cpp:829)

Frame start (docs/08 section 1): SOM address 0, then two zero words (0035, 0039) hold the header's place; DM 001E = 1 is the address of the last word written, DM 002B/002A/0108 = 0 (0108 counts objects for the draw-order nodes), DM 0958 and 002D/002E = 0 (polygon count, overflow flag).
/SOMCLK = 0: the list starts at word 0 of the bank the 68k does not see (case 3, harddriv_m.cpp:815)
SOMLATCH word 0 = 0: placeholder for N, written at 00BE (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH word 1 = 0: placeholder for T, written at 00C0

entries.name: next_object
entries.comment: Per-object loop: counts objects in DM 0030; 0097 and 00B3 jump back here.

entries.name: batch_handshake
entries.comment: Before each entry: when its flags word (word 23, I5 = DM 001B + 17h at 0043-0046) has bit 14 set, the count of entries done (DM 0030) goes to DM 1FE3, /GINT interrupts the 68k (004C) and the ADSP waits until the 68k clears DM 1FE3 (004D-004F). docs/07 section 3.
/GINT: interrupt the 68k at level 2 (case 6, harddriv_m.cpp:823)

entries.name: read_object_list
entries.comment: Reads the next 24-word entry of the object list the 68k wrote at DM 0A00 (pointer DM 001B; docs/07 section 3 has the fields). Word 0 = FFFF ends the frame (0053 -> 00B4).
word 0 & 0FFF -> DM 001C and DM 0009: the near object number (the directory index, 009E)
word 1 & 0FFF -> DM 001D: the far object number, drawn when 06A1 sets DM 0017 (0098-009D)
words 2-10 -> DM 0000-0008: the object's rotation matrix (00F6 combines it with the camera's)
words 11-16 -> DM 001F-0024: the position x, y, z as 32-bit high/low pairs (06A1)
words 17-18 -> DM 000A-000B: the cull distance, 32 bits (06A1 at 06F3-06FE)
words 19-20 -> DM 0025-0026: the LOD distance, 32 bits (06A1 at 06FF-0708)
word 21 -> DM 000F: the bounding radius (06A1 frustum test, 0730)
word 22 -> DM 0027, sign-extended into DM 0028 (the 68k copies its entity's +36h here, 0x02E26A)

word 23, the flags, read without advancing: bit 15 -> DM 002C = 1 (CALL 0887 at 008C); bits 8-11 -> DM 002F, ORed into every face colour word (01CE); bit 14 is the batch handshake (0047); bit 0 is written back at 0094
CALL 06A1: cull and level of detail; DM 0013 = 1 when the object is drawn
DM 0013 into bit 0 of the flags word (for the 68k); a culled object (0) skips the object ROM (0097 -> 0040)
the object number: DM 0009 (near), or DM 001D (far) when DM 0017 is set

entries.name: read_object_pointer
entries.comment: Fetches the object's ROM address: /SIMCLK = the entry, /MP = 0, two NOPs, /SIMBUF read, then the word shifted left by 2 is split into a page (SR1 -> /MP) and an address (SR0 -> /SIMCLK). HYP: a word pointer in units of 4 words; M3 decodes it. [/SIMCLK: object ROM word address (hdadsp_special_w case 1, harddriv_m.cpp:807)]
/MP: object ROM page, base = 0x10000 * value (case 7, harddriv_m.cpp:829)
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)
/MP: object ROM page, base = 0x10000 * value (case 7, harddriv_m.cpp:829)
/SIMCLK: object ROM word address (hdadsp_special_w case 1, harddriv_m.cpp:807)
per object: CALL 00F6 (transform_matrix), 0114 (read_object_header), 0174 (read_object_records)
DM 002E set (by the SOM output, docs/08) ends the frame early

entries.name: end_frame
entries.comment: End of frame: the FFFF that ends the commands (00B5, word T = DM 001E + 1, kept in DM 0109), write_draw_order (080B) appends the table and its FFFF, then /SOMCLK 0 and the header: word 0 = N (the address of the last FFFF, DM 001E + 1 after 080B), word 1 = T. /GINT (00C1) with DM 1FE3 = 0 tells the 68k the list is complete (0x02E44A sets FF9BB4). docs/08.
SOMLATCH word T = FFFF: the end of the commands (GSP FFF44CA0 jumps over the commands with word 1 = T)
/SOMCLK = 0: back to the header
SOMLATCH word 0 = N = DM 001E + 1: the address of the final FFFF; the 68k copies N words from word 1 (0x02F0C2) and checks word N = FFFF (0x02F0E2)
SOMLATCH word 1 = T = DM 0109: where the commands end and the draw order begins (GSP FFF44CA0)
/GINT with DM 1FE3 = 0: the frame is done (68k h_level2_adsp -> 0x02E44A: FF9BB4 = 1)

entries.name: transform_matrix
entries.comment: Multiplies the object's rotation matrix (DM 0000-0008) by the camera matrix (PM 1000-1008, from DM 1FF5-1FFD) into PM 1010-1018, rounded (010B-010E). Used by 0114 for vertices and normals.

entries.name: read_object_header
entries.comment: Reads the object at the /MP page and /SIMCLK address 00A6-00A8 set. Header: 011C reads the point count (vertices + normals) into I0 and 011F overwrites it (never used); 011F the vertex count -> DM 0032; 0123 the normal count -> DM 08DA. Then the vertices (014C-015D) and normals (015E-0172) through /SIMBUF read indirectly (I0 = 2000, 0147). The last read (0172) is the record-list pointer, left in SI for 0174. docs/07 section 4.
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)

block floating point: the camera-space position (DM 08DB-08E0, three 32-bit values from 06A1 at 076C-077E) sets a common exponent SE (EXPADJ 012B-0131); 0137-0146 store the scaled translation in DM 000C-000E and SE + 1 in DM 0033
I0 = 2000, M0 = 0: every DM(I0,M0) read below is a /SIMBUF read (014C, 014F, 0152, 0155, 0163, 0166, 0172), the address advancing in the ROM, not in I0
/SIMBUF (indirect): vertex 1, x

entries.name: transform_vertices
entries.comment: Per vertex (DM 0032 times): x, y, z through /SIMBUF at 014F, 0152, 0155 (each loop reads one word ahead), shifted by SE into DM 0010-0012, times the combined matrix PM 1010-1018 plus the translation DM 000C-000E (0157-015C) into DM 010D + 3(i - 1): point i, i = 1..vertices.

entries.name: rotate_normals
entries.comment: Per normal (DM 08DA times): x, y, z through /SIMBUF at 0163, 0166, 0172 (one ahead), rotated by PM 1010-1018 and rounded (+ 4000h, >> 15 at 016C-0170), stored after the vertices: point vertices + j. The read at 0172 after the last normal returns the record-list pointer.

entries.name: read_object_records
entries.comment: Walks the record list: DM 0034 = its address (the word 0172 read), /SIMCLK (017B), two /SIMBUF reads (017F: the polygon address; 0182: type << 12 | count << 6 | colour), then JUMP (I4) at 0186 through record_type_table on the type. Type 0 returns: the end of the object. docs/07 section 4.
/SIMCLK: object ROM word address (hdadsp_special_w case 1, harddriv_m.cpp:807)
/SIMBUF: record word 0, the address of the face's polygon -> AX1
/SIMBUF: record word 1, type << 12 | count << 6 | colour; the type (>> 12, 0183) indexes record_type_table

entries.name: record_type_table
entries.comment: Entry n = PM 0187 + n: type 0 RTS (end of the record list), type 1 JUMP 0197, types 2-14 run through the NOPs to 0196, type 15 JUMP 0199. The ROM uses types 1 and 15 only (docs/07).

entries.name: record_unshaded
entries.comment: Type 1: DM 0038 = 1: the face skips shading (01C9 ORs 1000h into its colour) and the clipper takes the 068B path (0273-0276), the output 0663 (01D9).

entries.name: record_face
entries.comment: Types 1-15: the next record is this one + 2 (DM 0034, 019A-019B).
colour = word 1 & 3F -> DM 0036; colour 0 hides the face: 01E4 reads on from the record list to its first FFFF and the next record follows (DM 0035 is 1 from the record before)

count = (word 1 >> 6) & 3F, 0 meaning 1 -> DM 0035: polygons read in sequence for this record. Always 0 in the ROM; a count above 1 would read its next polygon at the last projected vertex's z + 1 in the object's page: 04B2 restores /MP (04DD-04DE) but not the /SIMCLK address
/SIMCLK = the polygon address (record word 0); /SIMCLK is the object ROM word address, hdadsp_special_w case 1, harddriv_m.cpp:807
CALL 01E8 (read_face_normal): AF >= 0, the face looks away: skip_polygon

entries.name: copy_polygon_vertices
entries.comment: Front-facing: the vertices after the first, until FFFF (/SIMBUF at 01B1, 01B2-01B3), each point's three camera-space words to DM 0043 on; DM 08EA keeps the largest z; I0 counts the vertices -> DM 0039 (01C2).

/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780); /SIMBUF read in the record loop: one word per iteration, NOT = FFFF ends it (01B2-01B3)

DM 08EA = the face's largest vertex z, clamped at 0: 01E8 cleared it and kept the first vertex's z if not negative (01EA-01EB, 020A-020E), 01B0-01C1 keep the largest z of the others (01BD-01BF). One value per face: the draw-order key of its command (0516, 066B; docs/08 section 1.5)
type 15 (DM 0038 = 0): CALL 0214 shades the face; type 1: colour |= 1000h (01C9-01CC)

DM 0036 OR DM 002F (01CD-01D0): the object entry's flags bits 8-11 (0082-0084; docs/07 section 3.1, which calls them the colour bank) ORed into the colour word: bits 8-9 reach the colour index, bits 10-11 are the command word's fill and this is their only source, so every face of an object gets the same fill (docs/08 sections 1.2, 4.3)
hand-over to the clipper 0271, the projection 04B2 and the SOM output 0663 / 04EB (docs/08, M3b)
next polygon of the record (DM 0035 - 1 > 0: 01A8), else the next record (017A)
/SIMBUF until FFFF: the rest of a face that looks away, or (from 019F) a colour-0 face's record list words.
entries.name: skip_polygon
read_face_normal
entries.comment: Reads the face's normal point (/SIMBUF 01EC) into DM 0014-0016 and its first vertex (/SIMBUF 01FC) into DM 0040-0042 and DM 08E7-08E9; returns in AF the sign of normal . vertex in camera space (back-face test: >= 0 looks away); DM 08EA = the vertex z if positive.
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)
MR = n + n * 1: the ADSP-2100 multiplier works in fractional mode and shifts the product left by one, so MR0 = 3n; + 010A: point n starts at DM 010A + 3n (point 1 at 010D)
/SIMBUF read: the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances (hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780)

entries.name: shade_face
entries.comment: Type-15 faces: colour >= 1F: colour & 1F, flat. Otherwise intensity = normal . (PM 1019-101B + PM 101C-101E) + 2D41h (0221-022A: CNTR = 2, three MACs per pass, L3 = 3 wraps I3 over DM 0014-0016; HYP: two light vectors, filled from DM 1FEF-1FF4 at 001B-0020), 0 if negative, faded by depth_fade (0238), times 12h (022F-0230) -> colour word (colour << 4) + 10h | intensity (HYP: a ramp per colour; M3b decodes the colour word).
Colours 1Fh and up (DM 0036 >= 1Fh, 021C-021D) are not lit: 021E-021F store DM 0036 AND 1Fh and return, so a record colour of 20h-3Fh reaches the command word as 00h-1Fh (docs/08 section 1.2).

entries.name: depth_fade
entries.comment: DM 1FE6 = 0: off. Otherwise scales the intensity DM 003A by the face's largest z (DM 08EA) against DM 1FE7-1FE8 (HYP: fog with distance).

entries.name: project_vertices
entries.comment: Projects the polygon's DM(0039) points, (X, Y, z) triples read from the address DM 0928 holds (04B3 I0 = DM(0928), set to 0040 at 0272/0283 and moved by the clipper at 02C8, 031F, 0385, 03EB, 0452), into (x, y) pairs at DM 0040: x = FFh + X * r, y = FFh - Y * r (AR = -SR1 at 04C4 / 04E0, products 04C6-04CA), where r is one /SIMBUF read with /MP = 1 (04BC) and /SIMCLK = z (04C2): entry z of the reciprocal table (object ROM page 1, words 0000-7FFF, docs/07 section 5.1). z <= 200h takes 04E0 (read at 04E1, products shifted left 9), larger z reads at 04C5. DM 1FE4 nonzero rescales the results by DM 1FE4/1FE5 (04CB-04DC). /MP = DM 0031 again at 04DD-04DE; /SIMCLK is not restored.
/MP: object ROM page, base = 0x10000 * value (case 7, harddriv_m.cpp:829)
/SIMCLK: object ROM word address (hdadsp_special_w case 1, harddriv_m.cpp:807)

/SIMBUF read: the reciprocal table entry z (z > 200h: 2^24 / z); /SIMBUF returns the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances, hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780
/MP: object ROM page, base = 0x10000 * value (case 7, harddriv_m.cpp:829)

/SIMBUF read: the reciprocal table entry z (z <= 200h: 2^15 / z, product shifted left by 9 at 04E3-04E4); /SIMBUF returns the object ROM word at the /MP page + the /SIMCLK address, which then advances, hdadsp_special_r case 0, harddriv_m.cpp:780

entries.name: emit_polygon
entries.comment: Writes one polygon command to the SOM (docs/08 section 1.3): refuses when DM 001E + polygons (DM 002D) reaches 1FA4h or 1EAh polygons (DM 002E = 1, 04F3/04F9), clamps every coordinate to 0-1FFh (0509-050D), writes the command word (0515), inserts the draw-order node (CALL 07A2), finds the top vertex (052B-0544), walks the left and right chains down, one segment per vertex, and ends with FFFF FFFF (05D2/05D4).
clamps each projected coordinate (x and y alike) into 0-1FFh

SOMLATCH: the command word, DM 0036 = the record's colour and flags (0214 lights it: ((colour << 4) + 10h) OR shade, 0232-0235; 01CB/01CF OR in 1000h for image records and the object's DM 002F bits 8-11)
CALL insert_depth_node: key = DM 08EA (the face's largest vertex z, 01C3) >> DM 0033 (+ the object's DM 0027/0028), value = DM 001E (the command's address - 1)
finds the top vertex (smallest y): on a flat top, I1 (the left chain) takes the leftmost and I2 (the right chain) the rightmost of the top vertices (0537-0541); 0550-0563 step over a repeated vertex
the polygon header: x of the left chain's top vertex, x of the right chain's, and y (0565, 0567, 056B)
SOMLATCH: xl, the left edge's x on the top row (GSP B0, FFF450F0)
SOMLATCH: xr, the right edge's x on the top row (GSP A6, FFF45110)
SOMLATCH: y, the top row (GSP FFF45360)

segment loop 0575-05D0: the next vertex down on either chain ends the segment; 057A compares the two chains' next y and takes 057D (both end), 059D (the left one ends) or 05B7 (the right one ends); each case recomputes the slope of the chain that turned (05DD right, 0607 left) and writes one segment
segment (both chains end at the same y): right slope DM 003E/003F, left slope DM 003C/003D, count = dy + 1 (057D-057E)
SOMLATCH: right slope, low word (GSP A7 via FFF45510)
SOMLATCH: right slope, high word
SOMLATCH: left slope, low word (GSP A9 via FFF455A0)
SOMLATCH: left slope, high word
SOMLATCH: the row count, dy + 1 (GSP A10, FFF45610)
I7 += 5: the command's length in words, added to DM 001E at 05D9
segment (the left chain's vertex comes first): same five words, count from the left chain (059D-059E)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
segment (the right chain's vertex comes first): same five words (05B7-05B8)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
SOMLATCH: a word to the SOM output buffer at the SOM address, which then advances (case 2, harddriv_m.cpp:811)
FFFF FFFF ends the polygon (GSP FFF45520 compares the first long with FFFFFFFF); DM 001E += I7 (the words written)
SOMLATCH: FFFF, first half of the end marker
SOMLATCH: FFFF, second half

entries.name: right_slope
entries.comment: DM 003E/003F = (x of the right chain's next vertex - x of its current) * PM(1036 + dy): a signed 16.16 step per row. PM 1036-1235 holds floor(8000h/dy) for dy <= 40h and floor(200000h/dy) above (reciprocal_table); the fractional-mode product MR = AR * MY0 (SU) (05F1, 0601) doubles it, and dy > 40h shifts it right arithmetically by 6 (0602-0603): dx * 2*floor(8000h/dy), or (dx * 2*floor(200000h/dy)) >> 6 above 40h. About dx * 10000h / dy, but the reciprocal is truncated before the multiply (dx = 1, dy = 3: 5554h, not 5555h).

entries.name: left_slope
entries.comment: DM 003C/003D: the same slope for the left chain (I4/I1; MR = AR * MY0 (SU) at 061B/062B, the shift at 062C-062D): dx * 2*floor(8000h/dy), or (dx * 2*floor(200000h/dy)) >> 6 above 40h.

entries.name: restore_index_regs
entries.comment: Reloads I0-I7, M0-M7, L0-L7 from DM 0929-0940 (saved by 064A).

entries.name: save_index_regs
entries.comment: Saves I0-I7, M0-M7, L0-L7 into DM 0929-0940.

entries.name: emit_image
entries.comment: Writes an image command (record type 1, DM 0038 = 1; docs/08 section 1.4): the command word (066A, with bit 12), the draw-order node (CALL 07A2), then the DM(0039) projected corner points as (x, y) pairs (0678/067A) and FFFF FFFF (0680/0682). Unclamped. GSP FFF48FC0 draws it.
SOMLATCH: the image command word (bit 12 set at 01CB; bits 0-5 select the image, GSP FFF491B0)
SOMLATCH: a corner's x
SOMLATCH: a corner's y
SOMLATCH: FFFF, the end marker's first half
SOMLATCH: FFFF, second half

For image records (called from 0276, before the projection): AF = 1 when any point's z (every third word from DM 0042) is below C8h; then DM 0039 = 0 and the image is dropped (HYP: a near-plane cull).

entries.name: cull_and_lod
entries.comment: Per entry: position (DM 001F-0024) minus the camera (PM 1009-100E) into DM 0941-0946; a distance estimate into DM 0947-0948 (06C2-06F2); not below the cull distance (DM 000A-000B): culled, DM 0013 = 0 (06FC); DM 0017 = 1 when not below the LOD distance (DM 0025-0026: the far object); the offset rotated into camera space (0739-074E) and tested against the view with the radius DM 000F (074F-076B); camera-space position into DM 08DB-08E0 for 0114 (076C-077E).

entries.name: init_0780
entries.comment: Called from reset (0004) and at the start of every frame (003D): sets M and L registers and constants (HYP; M3).

entries.name: insert_depth_node
entries.comment: Inserts a 6-word node at DM 0956 into the doubly linked list in PM between the head PM 123C and the tail PM 1242: +0/+1 the 32-bit key SR (depth; the first object, DM 0030 = 0, gets 10000000h, 07B4), +2 previous, +3 next, +4 the object number DM 0108, +5 the value AY0 = the command's address - 1. The key is per command (the face's largest vertex z, 01C3, shifted by DM 0033, plus the object's bias), so the list orders faces, not objects. The walk starts from the previous node inserted (DM 0957) and runs towards the head or the tail (07D8/07F4), comparing not the key but the key - 10h (07C1-07C5): a new node goes in after neighbours whose keys are up to 10h below its own, so the list is ordered by key only to within 10h, each key at most 10h above the one before it (MAME: make depthkeys, docs/08 section 1.5; HYP that the head end is the farthest; the GSP draws in list order).

SR = the key - 10h (07C1-07C5), after the key itself is stored (07BD/07BE): every comparison of the walk (07D5/07D6, 07D9/07DC, 07F5/07F8) uses it, so the list is ordered by key only to within 10h (MAME: make depthkeys, docs/08 section 1.5)

entries.name: write_draw_order
entries.comment: Appends the draw order to the SOM: from the head's next (PM 123F) to the tail (PM 1242), writes each node's +5 word (the command's address - 1) through I2 = 2002h, M0 = 0 (0828), counts them in MR (fractional mode: 2 per node, halved at 082C), then FFFF (082B) and DM 001E += count + 1.
SOMLATCH (I2 = 2002h): a table entry, the command's address - 1 (GSP FFF45040: the command is at the list's word 1 + entry)
SOMLATCH: FFFF, the end of the table and of the list (word N)

entries.name: init_0834
entries.comment: Called after 0780 (0005, 003E): fills data RAM from 0959 with FFFF/7FFF (HYP: clears the SOM sort buckets; M3).

entries.name: entry_flag15
entries.comment: Called when the entry's flags bit 15 set DM 002C (0081, 008C): runs DM 08DB through 0869, 087A and 0847 before the object is read (HYP: an extra transform of the position; not decoded).

entries.name: pm_tables
entries.comment: PM 1029-1235, loaded by the last two records (68k records 1029/0D and 1036/200). PM 1029-1035 disassembles as noise, read as data (HYP: a table); PM 1036-1235 is reciprocal_table (docs/08 section 1.3). PM 1000-1028 is the workspace that 0018 fills.

entries.name: reciprocal_table
entries.comment: PM 1036-1235 (loaded, 68k record 1036/200): 200h words, entry dy = floor(8000h/dy) for dy <= 40h, floor(200000h/dy) above (the 16 high bits of each 24-bit word are what MY0 reads). right_slope/left_slope (05E0, 060A) index it with the segment's dy. Data, not code.
